evidence: Receiving P assay t=48h: 3.10 g/L vs sources 3.06/3.02/2.98 g/L — batch on nominal trajectory
Receiving DO2 at t=52h ~10.8 mg/L, min observed ~8.5 mg/L (t~24h dip), all far above 2.0 mg/L limit
Source batches show product decline after ~72h (P: 8.36→7.89→6.85 g/L at 96h) despite continued feed-driven volume growth
Forward model: keep=576 kg, reduce_feed=596 kg, combined=596 kg, strong_feed_reduction=621 kg (range 616–627, all 5 sensitivity members feasible)
Model min DO2 under strong_feed_reduction: 9.81 mg/L (range 8.71–10.67), no oxygen deficit (below_limit_h=0)
args.rationale: The receiving batch matches the source trajectory closely (P 3.10 g/L at 48h vs sources ~3.0; DO2 ~10.8 mg/L at 52h; identical 24h DO2 dip/recovery pattern) and shows no oxygen stress. However, the source-calibrated physical model shows that product mass declines late in the batch while feed continues to dilute volume, so a strong feed reduction (0.6x) retains more product mass at harvest: 621 kg vs 576 kg for KEEP, with all sensitivity members feasible and minimum DO2 of ~8.7-10.7 mg/L, far above the 2.0 mg/L constraint. Air increase offers no benefit (no O2 deficit exists), stop yields zero production. Chosen to maximize retained product mass without oxygen-constraint risk.
args.uncertainty: The forward model is source-calibrated and imperfect; the hidden receiving realization may differ (transfer multiplier estimated 0.979, cost 2.35). If the receiving batch deviates from source kinetics more than observed data suggests, the ~45 kg mass gain of strong reduction could shrink or reverse; however, oxygen feasibility margins are large (min DO2 >8.5 mg/L across all actions and sensitivity members), so downside risk is limited to modest yield loss, not constraint violation.
